The walk is only partly consistent with the stated triangle, so this answer rests on one assumption. I tracked each vertex as (row, column), with the top at (0,0). The moves are:

- down-left: (r+1, c)
- down-right: (r+1, c+1)
- up-left: (r−1, c−1)
- up-right: (r−1, c)
- left: (r, c−1)
- right: (r, c+1)

Early on, the walk steps from (2,1) right by two to (2,3) and up-left to (1,2), which lie outside a triangle with ≤ r+1 vertices per row. I assumed these overshoots do not matter and kept the same coordinates, since the walk lands on valid, consistent vertices afterwards. That assumption could not be checked.

- can (2,1), tart (3,2), cake (4,3), bed (5,4)
- strawberry (6,5), bear (7,5), pen (7,6), cucumber (6,6)

The final segment starts at tube (9,5):
- down-right twice gives (11,7)
- up-left two gives (9,5)
- down-left gives (10,5)
- stay at (10,5)
- left gives (10,4)
- down-left two gives (12,4)
- up-right twice gives (11,4), then (10,4)

The final position (10,4) is the vertex where the soap was seen.

Final answer: soap
